The strong relationship between the Maldives and China, firmly grounded in our unwavering commitment to the One China Principle, continues to yield mutual benefits to both our nations. As we cast our gaze towards the future, it is with renewed optimism I reaffirm our dedication to further deepening this partnership and collaborating closely on matters of shared interest on the global stage.

I look forward to continuing to work closely with Your Excellency to build upon the positive momentum in our relations. May the people of China continue to experience peace, progress, and prosperity, and may the bonds of friendship between our two countries flourish even further in the coming years.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration”

en.title: State Minister Khaleel highlights the priority areas for the Maldives during the 78th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, at the General Debate
en.description: State Minister Khaleel highlights the priority areas for the Maldives during the 78th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, at the General Debate
en.body:
State Minister Khaleel highlights the priority areas for the Maldives during the 78th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, at the General Debate

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel highlighted the priority areas for the Maldives during the 78th session of the United Nations General Assembly, speaking during the General Debate today.

These priorities were identified as: equal representation in the multilateral system, addressing the climate crisis, the achievement of sustainable development through affordable financing, ensuring gender equality, promotion and protection of human rights and upholding the peace and security of the international fora.

State Minister Khaleel highlighted the negative impacts of climate change on Small Island Developing States like the Maldives, and the need to work together nationally and internationally to fight climate change, especially during the upcoming COP28. He reiterated the importance of concessional financing for developing countries. and called for the early adoption and use of the Multidimensional Vulnerability Index.

The statement also underlined the work that has been carried out by the Maldives in addressing gender equality, such as the initiative by the Maldives delegation to establish the International Day of Women in Diplomacy, the active participation in the Human Rights Council and the ratification of the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance.

State Minister Khaleel concluded the statement by reiterating Maldives’ support for the State of Palestine and called for a sovereign and independent state established on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its Capital. He also noted the importance of countering terrorism and violent extremism in creating a peaceful and stable future.

The Maldives delegation to the 78th Session of the United Nations General Assembly is led by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel. Minister of Health Ahmed Naseem and a delegation of Officials of the Ministry of Health, and a delegation from the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Technology, also participated in various high level meetings held during the High Level week.

ENDS

en.title: Joint Press Release to reaffirm the decision to restore diplomatic ties between the Republic of Maldives and the Islamic Republic of Iran
en.description: Joint Press Release to reaffirm the decision to restore diplomatic ties between the Republic of Maldives and the Islamic Republic of Iran
en.body:
Joint Press Release to reaffirm the decision to restore diplomatic ties between the Republic of Maldives and the Islamic Republic of Iran

Following a meeting on Friday, 22 September 2023, between H.E. Mr Ahmed Khaleel, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives and H.E. Dr. Amir-Abdollahian, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, on the sidelines of the 78th Session of the UN General Assembly, the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Republic of Maldives, in alignment with the interests and aspirations of their peoples, reaffirmed their decision to restore diplomatic relations.

The two Governments have agreed to further develop the friendly relations between the two countries on the basis of mutual respect for sovereignty, equality, mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence.

Both countries have resolved to strengthen cooperation on a wide range of areas including investment, trade, seamless of travel and people-to-people contact, science, and technological innovation.

en.description: Maldives and Guyana sign a Visa Waiver Agreement and MOU on Political Consultations
en.body:
Maldives and Guyana sign a Visa Waiver Agreement and MOU on Political Consultations

*New York*

The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Co-operative Republic of Guyana signed the Agreement on Mutual Exemption of Visa Requirements, today. The Agreement allows for the exemption of visas for single or multiple entry for both countries' nationals, for a period of 30 days.

Both Governments also signed the Memorandum of Understanding on Political Consultations, to establish a framework for expanding cooperation and exchanges in areas of mutual interest.

The agreements were signed on behalf of the Government of Maldives by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, and on behalf of the Government of Guyana by the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Hugh Hilton Todd.

During the discussions following the signing ceremony, State Minister Khaleel expressed his gratitude to Minister Todd and the Government of Guyana for the commitment towards enhancing the cooperation between the two countries and desire to continue to explore new avenues for collaboration. State Minister Khaleel also expressed hope that the signing of these agreements will deepen the engagements and facilitate greater people-to-people contact.”

en.description: The Maldives and Togo sign a Visa Waiver Agreement
en.body:
The Maldives and Togo sign a Visa Waiver Agreement

The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Togo have signed an Agreement on Mutual Exemption of Visa Requirements today. Within the framework of this agreement, Maldivians with all types of passports will be able to travel to Togo without a visa and stay for up to 30 days.

The agreement was signed on behalf of the Government of Maldives by His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, and on behalf of the Government of Togo, by His Excellency Prof. Robert Dussey, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Integration and Togolese Abroad, at a signing ceremony held at the Permanent Mission of the Maldives in New York.

During the discussions following the signing ceremony, State Minister Khaleel thanked the Government of Togo for its commitment towards strengthening the bilateral relations with the Maldives and conveyed hope that the visa waiver agreement will increase the avenues for cooperation and people- to-people contact between the Maldives and Togo. Minister Dussey expressed keen interest in strengthening the bilateral ties with the Maldives and commitment to work together on areas of mutual interest.

ENDS

dv.description: ދިވެހިސަރުކާރާއި ޓޯގޯ ސަރުކާރާ ދެމެދު ވިސާ ވެއިވަރ އެއްބަސްވުމެއްގައި ސޮއިކޮށްފި
dv.body:
ދިވެހިސަރުކާރާއި ޓޯގޯ ސަރުކާރާ ދެމެދު ވިސާ ވެއިވަރ އެއްބަސްވުމެއްގައި ސޮއިކޮށްފި

ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ޓޯގޯ ސަރުކާރާ ދެމެދު މިއަދު "އެގްރީމަންޓް އޮން މިއުޗުއަލް އެގްޒެމްޝަން އޮފް ވިސާ ރިކުއަޔަރމަންޓްސް" ގައި ސޮއިކޮށްފިއެވެ. މި އެއްބަސްވުމުގެދަށުން، ދިވެހިންނަށް ވިސާއާ ނުލައި ޓޯގޯއަށް ދަތުރުކޮށް، އެ ޤައުމަށް އެތެރެވާ ދުވަހުން ފެށިގެން ގިނަވެގެން 30 ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަކަށް އެ ޤައުމުގައި ތިބެވޭނެއެވެ. އަދި ހަމަ އެފަދައިން ޓޯގޯ ރައްޔިތުނަށްވެސް ވިސާނެގުމެއްނެތި 30 ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަކަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނެއެވެ.

މިއަދު އެމެރިކާގެ ނިއުޔޯކްގައި ހުންނަ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޕަރމަނަންޓް މިޝަންގައި ބޭއްވި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި، ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުގެ ފަރާތުން މި އެއްބަސްވުމުގައި ސޮއިކުރެއްވީ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ސްޓޭޓް ފޯ ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އަލްފާޟިލް އަޙުމަދު ޚަލީލްއެވެ.އަދި ޓޯގޯ ސަރުކާރުގެ ފަރާތުން ސޮއިކުރެއްވީ އެ ޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ހިޒް އެކްސަލަންސީ ޕްރޮފެސަރ ރޮބަޓް ޑުސޭއެވެ.

މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ވާހަކަފުޅުދައްކަވަމުން، ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ގުޅުން ބަދަހިކުރުމަށް ޓޯގޯ ސަރުކާރުން ދެއްވާ އެއްބާރުލުމަށް ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވައި، މި އެއްބަސްވުމުގެ ސަބަބުން ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ރައްޔިތުން އެއް ޤައުމުން އަނެއް ޤައުމަށް ފަސޭހަކަމާކާއެކު ދަތުރުކޮށް، ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައި އޮންނަ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާވެގެންދާނޭކަމަށް އުއްމީދުކުރަައްވާކަމަށް ސްޓޭޓް މިނިސްޓަރ އަޙުމަދު ޚަލީލްވަނީ ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ. އަދި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޑުސޭވެސްވަނީ ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ފައިދާހުރި ކަންތައްތަކެއް ކުރުމުގެ މަގު މި އެއްބަސްވުމުގެ ސަބަބުން ފަހިގެންދާނެކަމަށް ވިދާޅުވެފައެވެ.

The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Honduras signed the Agreement on Mutual Exemption of Visa Requirements, today. The Agreement allows for the exemption of visas for single or multiple entry for both countries' nationals, for a period of 30 days.

The agreement was signed on behalf of the Government of the Republic of Maldives by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, and on behalf of the Government of the Republic of Honduras by the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Eduardo Enrique Reina García.

During the discussions following the signing ceremony, State Minister Khaleel expressed his gratitude to the Government of the Republic of Honduras for its commitment towards enhancing the cooperation between the two countries and expressed hope that the signing of this agreement will enable greater people-to-people contact and further the engagements.

en.title: The General Debate of the 78th Session of the General Assembly Commences

The General Debate of the 78th Session of the General Assembly Commences

The General Debate of the 78th Session of the General Assembly opened today. A high-level delegation from the Maldives, led by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel, attended the opening.

Speaking at the opening, Secretary-General António Guterres stated that amid the complex global challenges, peace is inextricably linked to sustainable development. He called to renew multilateral institutions based on 21st Century economic and political realities, as the way forward to address the global crises. Further, Secretary-General called on world leaders to strengthen efforts to invest in climate action and promote gender equality for effective outcomes. The President of the 78th General Assembly, Dennis Francis, emphasised the need to unite with conviction and solidarity of global action to accelerate progress on achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.

The General Debate of the 78th Session of the General Assembly will be held from Tuesday, 19th September to Tuesday, 26th September. Heads of State and Governments and heads of national delegations will deliver statements at the General Debate under the theme, “Rebuilding trust and reigniting global solidarity: Accelerating action on the 2030 Agenda and its Sustainable Development Goals towards peace, prosperity, progress and sustainability for all”.

As Head of Delegation, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Khaleel is scheduled to deliver the statement from Maldives.

Maldives to Participate in the 54th Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council

The 54th Session of the UN Human Rights Council began today in Geneva, Switzerland. The session will be held from 11 September 2023 to 13 October 2023.

In line with the Government’s key policies and priorities, the Maldives delegation will deliver national statements under several agenda items.

The Maldives will also be delivering two joint statements on behalf of Small Island Developing States (SIDS) based in Geneva. The first, to be presented during the Interactive Dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on water and sanitation, will address the importance of access to clean water and sanitation for SIDS and highlight the challenges they face in ensuring these basic rights. The second, to be made during the Biennial Panel Discussion on Youth and Human Rights, will emphasize the significance of youth empowerment in the context of climate change.

The Maldives delegation for the 54th Session of the Human Rights Council will be led by Dr. Asim Ahmed, Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Offices at Geneva. The delegation will include, Mr. Adam Hamid, Counsellor of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva, Ms. Aminath Shifaya Ibrahim, Counsellor of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva, Ms. Maryam Fathika Fayaz, Second Secretary of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva and Ms. Mizna Waheed, Third Secretary of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva.

The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe have signed an Agreement on Mutual Exemption of Visa Requirements today. Within the framework of this agreement, Maldivians with all types of passports will be able to travel to São Tomé and Príncipe without a visa and stay for up to 90 days.

The Agreement was signed on behalf of the Government of Maldives by Her Excellency Aishath Azeema, Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives to the People’s Republic of China, and on behalf of the Government the Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe, by Her Excellency Isabel Maysa Jesus da Graca Domingos, Ambassador of the Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe to the People’s Republic of China, at a signing ceremony held at the Embassy of Maldives in Beijing.

During the discussions following the signing ceremony, Ambassador Aishath Azeema thanked the Government of São Tomé and Príncipe for its commitment towards strengthening the existing bilateral relations between the two countries and conveyed hope that the signing of this agreement will increase the avenues for engagement and people to people contact between the Maldives and São Tomé and Príncipe. Ambassador Domingos also expressed keen interest in strengthening the bilateral ties with the Maldives and assured São Tomé and Príncipe’s commitment to work with the Maldives on areas of mutual interest.

ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ސާއޯ ޓުމޭ އެންޑް ޕްރިންސިޕޭ ސަރުކާރާ ދެމެދު މިއަދު "އެގްރީމަންޓް އޮން މިއުޗުއަލް އެގްޒެމްޝަން އޮފް ވިސާ ރިކުއަޔަރމަންޓްސް" ގައި ސޮއިކޮއްފިއެވެ. މި އެއްބަސްވުމުގެދަށުން، ދިވެހިންނަށް ވިސާއާ ނުލައި ސާއޯ ޓުމޭ އެންޑް ޕްރިންސިޕޭއަށް ދަތުރުކޮށް، އެ ޤައުމަށް އެތެރެވާ ދުވަހުން ފެށިގެން ގިނަވެގެން 90 ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަކަށް އެ ޤައުމުގައި ތިބެވޭނެއެވެ. އަދި ހަމަ އެފަދައިން ސާއޯ ޓުމޭ އެންޑް ޕްރިންސިޕޭ ރައްޔިތުނަށްވެސް ވިސާނެގުމެއްނެތި 90 ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަކަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނެއެވެ.

މިއަދު ބެއިޖިންގގައި ހުންނަ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އެމްބަސީގައި ބޭއްވި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި، މި އެއްބަސްވުމުގައި ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުގެ ފަރާތުން ސޮއިކުރެއްވީ ޗައިނާއަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު އަލްފާޟިލާ ޢާއިޝަތު ޢަޒީމާއެވެ. އަދި ސާއޯ ޓުމޭ އެންޑް ޕްރިންސިޕޭ ސަރުކާރުގެ ފަރާތުން ސޮއިކުރެއްވީ ޗައިނާއަށް އެ ޤައުމުން ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު ހަރ އެކްސަލަންސީ އިޒަބެލް މައިސާ ދަ ގްރާސާ ދޮމިންގޮސްއެވެ.

މި އެއްބަސްވުމުގައި ސޮއިކުރުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ވާހަކަފުޅުދައްކަވަމުން ސަފީރު އައިޝަތު އަޒީމާވަނީ، ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމަށް ސާއޯ ޓުމޭ އެންޑް ޕްރިންސިޕޭ ސަރުކާރުން ދެއްވާ އެއްބާރުލުމަށް ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވާކަމަށާއި މިއަދު ސޮއިކުރެވުނު އެއްބަސްވުމާއެކު ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ރައްޔިތުން އެއް ޤައުމުން އަނެއް ޤައުމަށް ފަސޭހަކަމާކާއެކު ދަތުރުކޮށް، ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާވެގެންދާނޭކަމަށް އުއްމީދުކުރަައްވާކަމަށް ވިދާޅުވެފައެވެ. އަދި އެމްބެސަޑަރ ދޮމިންގޮސްވެސްވަނީ ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ހަރަދުދަނާކޮށް ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ފައިދާހުރި ކަންތައްތަކެއް ކުރުމުގެ މަގު މި އެއްބަސްވުމުގެ ސަބަބުން ފަހިގެންދާނެކަމަށް ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ.

en.title: Minister Shahid meets with United States Senator Chris Van Hollen
en.description: Minister Shahid meets with United States Senator Chris Van Hollen
en.body:
Minister Shahid meets with United States Senator Chris Van Hollen

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid met Senator Christopher Van Hollen Jr of the United States Senate, today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid welcomed the Senator to the Maldives and reflected on the significance of the visit, which marked the first ever official visit from a Congressional Delegation.

The discussions between Minister Shahid and Senator Van Hollen focused on a wide range of issues, including digital infrastructure and cyber security, defence and security, democracy and good governance and human resource development.

Both Minister Shahid and Senator Van Hollen agreed on the need to increase higher education opportunities from American universities and academic exchanges between the two countries and reiterated commitments towards achieving it.

Before concluding the meeting, Minister Shahid extended a special gratitude to the Senator for his late father’s contribution to the advancement of Maldives-US partnership during his tenure as the Ambassador of the United States of America to the Maldives, serving from 10 December 1972 – 26 April 1976.

Minister Shahid was accompanied at the meeting by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel, Foreign Secretary Ahmed Latheef, Ambassador of the Maldives to the United States of America Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, Secretary, Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed, Secretary, Economic Cooperation Dr. Hussain Niyaaz, Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed, Director Adam Hamid and Desk Officer Saifulla Waleed.

ENDS

en.title: Visa Exemption for Maldivians travelling to Kyrgyz Republic
en.description: Visa Exemption for Maldivians travelling to Kyrgyz Republic
en.body:
Visa Exemption for Maldivians travelling to Kyrgyz Republic

Maldivian nationals travelling to Kyrgyz Republic will be exempted from visa effective today, 20 August 2023. The visa exemption will allow Maldivians holding valid Diplomatic, Official and Ordinary passports to enter and stay in Kyrgyz Republic a maximum period of thirty (30) days from the day of their entry.

In accordance with the visa exemption agreement signed between the two countries on 23 September 2022, Maldivians intending to stay for a longer period or to work or to attend an educational institution or conduct business in Kyrgyz Republic, will need to obtain an appropriate visa prior to travel.

ENDS

en.title: High Commissioner of Maldives to Brunei Darussalam presents Credentials to His Majesty the Sultan of Brunei Darussalam
en.description: High Commissioner of Maldives to Brunei Darussalam presents Credentials to His Majesty the Sultan of Brunei Darussalam
en.body:
High Commissioner of Maldives to Brunei Darussalam presents Credentials to His Majesty the Sultan of Brunei Darussalam

The non-resident High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to Brunei Darussalam, His Excellency Ali Hussain Didi presented his credentials to His Majesty Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Mu’izzadin Waddaulah ibni Al-Marhum Sultan Haji Omar ‘Ali Saifuddien Sa’adul Khair Waddien on Saturday, 19 August 2023 at Istana Nurul Iman, Bandar Seri Begawan.

The High Commissioner was received in audience by His Majesty the Sultan following the submission of his Credentials. During the audience, the High Commissioner conveyed best wishes from His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, President of the Republic of Maldives to His Majesty the Sultan, for his good health and happiness as well as for peace, prosperity, and happiness of the people of Brunei Darussalam. The Sultan congratulated the High Commissioner on his appointment and assured the full support and cooperation from the Government of Brunei Darussalam in discharging his responsibilities in his capacity as High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to Brunei Darussalam.

The High Commissioner conveyed his gratitude to the people and Government of Brunei Darussalam for their support to the Maldives, as we continue to strengthen the friendly relations between both countries.

In his non-resident capacity, the High Commissioner will be discharging his duties from Kuala Lumpur, where he is stationed. The High Commissioner was accompanied by First Secretary at the High Commission of Maldives in Malaysia, Mr. Munim Anees.

ENDS

en.title: The Maldives and Mongolia sign Visa Exemption Agreement
en.description: The Maldives and Mongolia sign Visa Exemption Agreement
en.body:
The Maldives and Mongolia sign Visa Exemption Agreement

The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of Mongolia today signed the Agreement on Mutual Exemption of Visa Requirements, which allows for the exemption of visa requirements for both country’s nationals, for a period of 30 days.

The agreement was signed on behalf of the Government of Maldives by His Excellency Ibrahim Shaheeb, High Commissioner of Maldives to India, and on behalf of the Government of Mongolia by His Excellency Ganbold Dambajav, Ambassador of Mongolia to Maldives. The signing ceremony was held in New Delhi, at the Embassy of Mongolia.

During the discussions at the signing ceremony, High Commissioner Shaheeb thanked the Government of Mongolia for its commitment towards strengthening the existing bilateral relations between the two countries and expressed hope that the signing of this agreement will facilitate avenues for engagement and people to people contact between the Maldives and Mongolia. Ambassador of Mongolia also expressed keen interest in strengthening the existing bilateral ties with the Maldives. He also reaffirmed their commitment to continue working closely in the multilateral arena.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs will issue a separate notification to inform citizens of the entry into force of the Agreement, once all internal procedures in both countries have been completed.

ENDS

en.title: The Maldives Ratifies the Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance
en.description: The Maldives Ratifies the Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance
en.body:
The Maldives Ratifies the Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance

The Maldives has ratified the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance (CED) by depositing the instrument of ratification at the United Nations headquarters in New York.

The Convention, adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on 20 December 2006, is one of the nine core international human rights treaties. CED came into effect on 23 December 2010, placing an obligation for States to prevent, prohibit and criminalize the offence of enforced disappearance as a grave human rights violation.

With this step forward, the Maldives becomes party to eight core international human rights treaties, marking the commitment of the Government to uphold human rights in both the domestic and international sphere.

The Maldives signed the CED on 6 February 2007. Of the 98 countries that have signed the Convention, 72 have ratified it thus far.

en.title: Maldivians to get visitor visa to Saudi Arabia
en.description: Maldivians to get visitor visa to Saudi Arabia
en.body:
Maldivians to get visitor visa to Saudi Arabia

On 6 August 2023, the Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia announced its decision to include Maldives in the list of countries eligible for visitor visa (e-visa and visa on arrival).

This decision by the Government of Saudi Arabia would enable Maldivians to obtain the visitor visa, either by completing the e-visa application online, or by applying for visa at the airport upon arrival at the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

Under the e-visa option, Maldivians will be eligible for a multiple entry visa that is valid for a year from the date of issue. Each visit under this visa allows for a stay not exceeding 90 days. The e-visa price is SAR 535 (about USD 142.45) and the application fee and medical insurance fee are included in the e-visa fee.

Under the visa on arrival option, Maldivians will be eligible for multiple or single entry visa (depending on the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs). The visa on arrival fee is SAR 300 (about USD 80), with an additional medical insurance fee of SAR 180 (about USD 48.03)

The visitor visa is applicable for the purpose of tourism, umrah, business, and visiting relatives and friends. It does not allow working for a wage or performing Umrah during Hajj.

The decision of the Government of Saudi Arabia to include the Maldives in the list of countries eligible for e-visa or on-arrival visa demonstrates the closeness and priority accorded to the Maldives by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and is proof that the brotherly relationship between the Maldives and Saudi Arabia will continue to reach new heights.

ENDS

dv.title: ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާއަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ވިޒިޓަރ ވީސާ ލިބޭނެ އިންތިޒާމް ސަޢުދީ ސަރުކާރުން ހަމަޖައްސަވައިފި
dv.description: ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާއަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ވިޒިޓަރ ވީސާ ލިބޭނެ އިންތިޒާމް ސަޢުދީ ސަރުކާރުން ހަމަޖައްސަވައިފި
dv.body:
ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާއަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ވިޒިޓަރ ވީސާ ލިބޭނެ އިންތިޒާމް ސަޢުދީ ސަރުކާރުން ހަމަޖައްސަވައިފި

ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާއަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހިންނަށް ވިޒިޓަރ ވިސާ (އީ-ވިސާ ނުވަތަ ވިސާ އޮން-އެރައިވަލް) ދެއްވުމަށް ސަޢޫދީ ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމަވައިފިއެވެ. އަދި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެވަނީ ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާއަށް ވިޒިޓަރ ވިސާ ލިބޭ ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ލިސްޓުގައި ހިމަނުއްވާފައެވެ.

މިގޮތަށް ސަޢޫދީ ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމެވުމާއެކު، ދިވެހިން ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާއަށް ދަތުރުކުރުމުގެ ކުރިން އޮންލައިންކޮށް، އިލެކްޓްރޯނިކް ޕޯޓަލް މެދުވެރިކޮށް އީ-ވިސާ ނެގުމުގެ ފުރުޞަތު އޮންނާނެއެވެ. ނުވަތަ ވިސާއާނުލާ އެ ޤައުމަށް ދަތުރުކޮށް އެއަރޕޯޓުން ވިސާ އޮން އެރައިވަލް ނެގުމުގެ ފުރުޞަތު އޮންނާނެއެވެ.

އީ-ވިސާގައި ދިވެހިންނަށް މަލްޓިޕަލް އެންޓްރީ އުޞޫލުން ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާއަށް ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނެއެވެ. އަދި 1 އަހަރު ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަކަށް މި ވިސާ ޞައްހަވާއިރު، ކޮންމެ އެންޓްރީއަކަށް ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާގައި ގިނަވެގެން 90 ދުވަސް ހޭދަކުރެވޭނެއެވެ. މި އީ-ވިސާގެ ފީއަކީ (މެޑިކަލް އިންޝޫރަންސް އަދި އެޕްލިކޭޝަން ހިމެނޭގޮތަށް 535 ސަޢޫދީ ރިޔާލް (ގާތްގަނޑަކަށް 142.45 އެމެރިކާ ޑޮލަރު) އެވެ.

ވިސާ އޮން-އެރައިވަލްގެ ދަށުން މަލްޓިޕަލް ނުވަތަ ސިންގަލް އެންޓްރީ ވިސާ ލިބޭނެއެވެ. މަލްޓިޕަލް އެންޓްރީ ނުވަތަ ސިންގަލް އެންޓްރީކަން ނިންމަވާނި ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާގެ ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓްރީންނެވެ. މި ވިސާގެ ފީއަކީ 300 ސަޢޫދީ ރިޔާލް (ގާތްގަނޑަކަށް 80 އެމެރިކާ ޑޮލަރު) އެވެ. އަދި މެޑިކަލް އިންޝޫރަންސަށް އިތުރު 180 ސަޢޫދީ ރިޔާލް (ގާތްގަނޑަކަށް 48.03 އެމެރިކާ ޑޮލަރު) ޚަރަދުވާނެއެވެ. ވިސާ އޮން-އެރައިވަލްގެ ދަށުން ދެއްވާ މަލްޓިޕަލް އެންޓްރީ ވިސާ 1 އަހަރު ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަކަށް ޞައްހަވާނެއެވެ.

ފަތުރުވެރިކަމަށާއި އުމްރާގެ އަޅުކަން އަދާކުރުމަށާއި ވިޔަފާރީގެ ބޭނުންތަކަށް، އަދި ރަހުމަތްތެރިންނާއި ގާތްތިމާގެ މީހުންނާ ބައްދަލުކޮށްލުމަށް އިސްވެ ދެންނެވުނު ވިޒިޓަރ ވިސާގެދަށުން ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނެއެވެ. ނަމަވެސް، ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާގައި އެއްވެސް އުޖޫރައެއް ލިބޭގޮތަށް މަސައްކަތްކުރުމަށާއި ޙައްޖުގެ ދުވަސްވަރު އުމްރާކުރުމަށް އެ ޤައުމަށް ދިއުމަށް މި ވިސާ ބޭނުން ނުކުރެވޭނޭކަމަށް ސަޢޫދީ ސަރުކާރުންވަނީ އަންގަވާފައެވެ.

ދިވެހިންނަށް ވިސާނެގުމުގައި މިފަދަ ލުއި ފަސޭހަ ގޮތެއް ސަޢޫދީ ސަރުކާރުން ހަމަޖައްސަވައިދެއްވުމަކީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ސަޢޫދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާއާ ދެމެދު އޮންނަ ގާތް އަޚުވަންތަކަމުގެ ގުޅުމާއި ސަޢޫދީ ސަރުކާރުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ދެއްވާ ޚާއްޞަ އަޙައްމިޔަތުކަން ރަމްޒުކޮށްދޭ ހެއްކެކެވެ.

en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Republic Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of North Macedonia

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sent a message of felicitations to Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Republic of North Macedonia Bujar Osmani, on the occasion of the Republic day of the Republic of North Macedonia.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

"On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Maldives, and on my own behalf, it gives me great pleasure to extend felicitations and best wishes to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of the Republic of North Macedonia, as you celebrate your Republic day.

I am confident that the relations between Maldives and North Macedonia will continue to prosper and strengthen in the years ahead.

Please accept, Your Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration as well as our best wishes for the continued peace, progress and prosperity of North Macedonia.”

en.title: Minister Shahid calls upon the international community to take stronger measures to stop the recurrence of acts of hatred against Islam
en.description: Minister Shahid calls upon the international community to take stronger measures to stop the recurrence of acts of hatred against Islam
en.body:
Minister Shahid calls upon the international community to take stronger measures to stop the recurrence of acts of hatred against Islam

The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, today virtually participated in the 18th Extraordinary Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The meeting, co-hosted by the Governments of Saudi Arabia, as Chair of the 14th Islamic Summit, and Iraq, discussed the repeated incidents of desecration and burning of the Holy Quran in Sweden and Denmark, and also the storming of the holy grounds of the Al-Aqsa Mosque by the Minister of National Security of Israel.

In his remarks, Minister Shahid strongly condemned the recent burning and desecration of the Holy Quran. He described this vile act that as one that hurts the sentiments of all Muslims, and as a clear violation of the right to freedom of expression. He further said that it would lead to the spread of hatred and divisions within societies. Noting the importance of standing together for respect and mutual understanding, he noted joint efforts that led to the adoption of the Human Rights Council resolution on “combating religious hatred that constitutes incitement to discrimination, hostility or violence”. He also pointed to the powerful example set by a Muslim individual, who chose not to burn the Torah and the Bible, despite being allowed to do so, describing his act as a true reflection of what Islam represents – peace and tolerance.

In addition to this, he also condemned the repeated violations of the holy grounds of Al-Aqsa Mosque in the occupied East Jerusalem. He reiterated that the Government of Maldives will continue to stand in solidarity with the Palestinians in their inalienable right to self-determination. He also reiterated the Maldives’ long-standing position that a sustainable peace in the Middle East can only be achieved from a two-state solution, with the establishment of an independent and sovereign State of Palestine, based on the pre-1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital.

At the conclusion of the meeting, a resolution entitled “Repeated Incident of Desecration of Copies al-Mushaf ash-Sharif in the Kingdoms of Sweden and Denmark” and a communique entitled “Regarding the storming of the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque by Israeli occupation government’s officials” were adopted, with Member States agreeing to work together to stop acts of hate against Islam.

ENDS

dv.title: އޯ.އައި.ސީ. އިން ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުންގެ ފެންވަރުގައި ބޭއްވި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދު ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވައިފި
dv.description: ސްވީޑަން އަދި ޑެންމާކްގައި މުޞްޙަފް އެންދުމާއި އަލް-އަޤްސާ މިސްކިތުގެ ހަރިންމަ ތެރެއަށް އިސްރޭލުގެ ނެޝަނަލް ސެކިއުރިޓީ މިނިސްޓަރ ވަނުމާ ގުޅިގެން އޯ.އައި.ސީ. އިން ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުންގެ ފެންވަރުގައި ބޭއްވި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދު ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވައިފި
dv.body:
ސްވީޑަން އަދި ޑެންމާކްގައި މުޞްޙަފް އެންދުމާއި އަލް-އަޤްސާ މިސްކިތުގެ ހަރިންމަ ތެރެއަށް އިސްރޭލުގެ ނެޝަނަލް ސެކިއުރިޓީ މިނިސްޓަރ ވަނުމާ ގުޅިގެން އޯ.އައި.ސީ. އިން ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުންގެ ފެންވަރުގައި ބޭއްވި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދު ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވައިފި

ދާދިފަހުން ސްވީޑަން އަދި ޑެންމާކްގައި ހުންނަ އިރާޤްގެ އެމްބަސީ ކުރިމަތީގައި މުޞްޙަފް އަންދާލި މައްސަލަ ކުށްވެރިކޮށް އެފަދަ އަމަލުތައް ތަކުރާރުވިޔަނުދިނުމަށް އެޅިދާނެ ފިޔަވަޅުތަކާ ގުޅޭގޮތުންނާއި އަލް-އަޤްސާ މިސްކިތުގެ ހަރިންމަ ތެރެއަށް އިސްރޭލުގެ ނެޝަނަލް ސެކިއުރިޓީ މިނިސްޓަރު ވަދެފައިވާތީ، އެކަން ކުށްވެރިކޮށް، ސައުދީ އަރަބިއްޔާ އަދި އިރާޤު ގެ ސަރުކާރުތަކުން އިސްވެ، އޯގަނައިޒޭޝަން އޮފް އިސްލާމިކް ކޯޕަރޭޝަންގެ (އޯ.އައި.ސީ.) ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުންގެ ފެންވަރުގައި މިއަދު ވަރޗުއަލްކޮށް ބޭއްވި އެކްސްޓްރާ-އޯޑިނަރީ ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދު، ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ތަޤްރީރު ކުރެއްވިއެވެ

މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ތަޤްރީރުކުރައްވަމުން މިނިސްޓަރ ޝާހިދު ވަނީ މުސްޙަފް އެންދުން ހަރުކަށި އިބާރާތުން ކުށްވެރިކޮށް، އެފަދަ އަމަލުތަކަކީ ހަރުކަށި ފިކުރުތައް ފެތުރުމަށް ބާރުއަޅާ އަމަލުތަކެއްކަމަށް ފާހަގަކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި، އެ އަމަލުތަކަކީ މުސްލިމް އުންމަތައް ލިބޭ ހިތާމައެއްގެ އިތުރުން، މުޖުތަމުޢު ބައިބައިކޮށް ފިތުނަ ފަސާދަ އުފެއްދުމަށް މަގުފަހިކޮށްދޭ ދަށުދަރަޖައިގެ ޢަމަލެއް ގޮތުގައިވެސް ސިފަކުރައްވާފައެވެ. ހަމައެއާއެކު، އިންސާނީ ހައްޤުގެ ނަމުގައި ދީނުގެ އަސާސްތަކުގެ ޚިލާފަށް ހިންގާ މިފަދަ އަމަލުތަކާ ދެކޮޅަށް ފިޔަވަޅުނާޅާ ދޫކޮށްލެވިގެން ދިއުމަކީ އެއްވެސް ހާލެއްގައި ޤަބޫލުކުރެވޭނެކަމެއްނޫން ކަމުގައިވެސް އެ މަނިކުފާނު ވިދާޅުވެފައިވެއެވެ. އެގޮތުން، އ.ދ.ގެ އިންސާނީ ހައްގުތަކާ ބެހޭ މަޖިލީހުން މި ހިނގާ ޖުލައި މަހު ފާސްކުރި ޤަރާރަކީ އެކުގައި މަސައްކަތްކޮށްގެން ލިބޭ ކާމިޔާބީއެއްގެ ދަލީލެއް ގޮތުގައިވެސް ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި، މިފަދަ އަމަލުތައް ހުއްޓުމަށް ސުލްހަމަސަލަސްކަން ދެމެހެއްޓުމަށާއި އިޚްތިރާމްކުރުމަށް ބާރުއެޅުމުގެ މުހިންމުކަންވެސް އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ ތަޤްރީރުގައި ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

މީގެ އިތުރުން، އަލް-އަޤްސާ މިސްކިތަށް އިސްރާއީލުން މެދުނުކެނޑި ދެމުންގެންދާ ހަމަލާތަކާއި، ހަރިންމަ ތެރެއަށް ހުއްޓުމެއްނެތި ވަނުންވެސް އެމަނިކުފާނު ކުށްވެރިކުރެއްވިއެވެ. މިފަދަ އަމަލުތަކަކީ މެދުއިރުމަތީގެ ސުލްހަމަސަލަސްކަން ގެއްލުވާލަ ފަދަ އަމަލެއްކަންވެސް ފާހަގަ ކުރެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި، އެ މަނިކުފާނުގެ ތަޤްރީރުގައި ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ރައްޔިތުން އަބަދުމެހެން ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނާއެކު ވާނެކަމުގައި ވިދާޅުވެ، ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ބިންތަކަށް އިސްރާއީލުން ވެރިވެގަތުން ނިމުމަކަށް ގެނެސް، ފަލަސްތީނުގެ މިނިވަން ދައުލަތެއް ޤާއިމްކޮށް، 1967 ވަނަ އަހަރުގެ ކުރީގެ ބޯޑަރާ ހިސާބަށް އިސްރާއީލުން ފަހަތަށް ޖެހުމަށް ބާރުއަޅާ، ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ދައުލަތުގެ ވެރިރަށުގެ ގޮތުގައި އިރުމަތީ ޤުދުސް އޮންނަން ޖެހޭ ކަމުގައި ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުވުން ނިމިގެންދިޔައީ އޯ.އައި.ސީ.ގެ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމުތަކުގެ މެދުގައި މި ދެ އަމަލުތައް ކުށްވެރިކޮށް، މެދުކެނޑުމެއްނެތި މަސައްކަތް ކުރާނެ ކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން ހާމަކޮށް، ދެ ޤަރާރެއްވެސް ފާސްކޮށްފައެވެ.

en.title: Ambassador of European Union pays farewell call on State Minister
en.description: Ambassador of European Union pays farewell call on State Minister
en.body:
Ambassador of European Union pays farewell call on State Minister

Ambassador of the European Union to the Maldives Denis Chaibi, paid a farewell call on Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, State Minister Khaleel expressed appreciation to Ambassador Chaibi for his remarkable efforts in strengthening the relations between the Maldives and the European Union. Furthermore, the State Minister and the Ambassador reviewed the existing cooperation and exchanged ideas aimed at further enhancing ties between the Maldives and the EU.

Ambassador Chaibi conveyed his gratitude to the Maldivian Government for the support extended during his tenure. He also reflected on EU's continuous assistance to the Maldives and acknowledged the remarkable progress made by the Government of Maldives especially in its efforts to combat the COVID-19 pandemic. Additionally, the Ambassador emphasized that the Maldives and the EU share similar views on various pressing global issues, including climate change and human rights.

State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed and Director Adam Hamid.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Throne Day greetings to the Kingdom of Morocco
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Throne Day greetings to the Kingdom of Morocco
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Throne Day greetings to the Kingdom of Morocco

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitations to the Minister of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccan Expatriates of the Kingdom of Morocco, Nasser Bourita on the occasion of the Throne Day of the Kingdom of Morocco.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It is my pleasure to extend warm greetings and felicitations to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Morocco, on the auspicious occasion of the Throne Day of the Kingdom of Morocco.

As you commemorate this joyous occasion, let me express our sincere hope that the brotherly relations between the Maldives and Morocco will continue to further strengthen in the years to come.

I also take this opportunity to convey my personal good wishes for Your Excellency’s good health and well-being and wish continued happiness and prosperity for the Kingdom of Morocco.

Please accept, Your Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

ENDS

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Vanuatu
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Vanuatu
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Vanuatu

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitations to Minister for Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and External Trade of Vanuatu, Jotham Napat on the occasion of their Independence Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and the people of the Maldives, I am delighted to extend sincere greetings to Your Excellency, the Government and to the people of Vanuatu on the occasion of your Independence Day.

As fellow Small Island Developing States (SIDS), I am committed to working together with you to tackle the most pressing regional and global challenges including the threat of climate change and to further strengthen our ties of friendship in the years to come.

Please accept, Your Excellency, the assurances of my highest regards and sincere wishes for your good health and happiness, as well as for continued progress and prosperity of the people of your country”.

en.description: Joint Press Release - Official Visit of the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan to the Maldives
en.body:
Joint Press Release - Official Visit of the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan to the Maldives

**Official Visit of His Excellency Hayashi Yoshimasa,**
**Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan to the Maldives**

**Joint Press Release**

30 July 2023

1. The Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan, Hayashi Yoshimasa paid an official visit to the Maldives from 29-30 July 2023 on the invitation of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives Abdulla Shahid. Minister Hayashi was accompanied by a high-level delegation from Japan.

2. Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid, and Foreign Minister Hayashi Yoshimasa, held bilateral discussions today.

3. During the Meeting, Minister Shahid welcomed Minister Hayashi and the delegation to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and highlighted the enduring strength of the Maldives-Japan partnership and the close people-to-people engagement and friendship that is the foundation of the relationship.

4. Both Foreign Ministers discussed a whole range of issues in the bilateral and multilateral spheres, including those related to Ukraine as well as Indo-Pacific region, and agreed to continue to work closely together to uphold and strengthen the free and open international order based on the rule of law, and to address shared interests, in further deepening the bilateral ties between the two countries.

5. Both Foreign Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen people to people exchanges, including on facilitating ease of travel between the two countries, and in promoting cultural cooperation.

6. On development cooperation, Minister Shahid thanked Minister Hayashi and the Japanese Government for the generous assistance provided to the Maldives over the years, including the construction of the seawall around the Capital City Male’, which is the most symbolic assistance provided by Japan.

7. Recalling that Japan have provided technical support for the mechanisation of fishing vessels, Minister Shahid conveyed gratitude to the Government of Japan for the important contribution for the development of the Maldives’ fisheries industry. Minister Shahid also underscored that Japan was instrumental in establishing the telecommunications infrastructure in the Maldives, which subsequently contributed immensely to the success of our world-renowned tourism industry.

8. Minister Shahid expressed his appreciation to Minister Hayashi and the Government of Japan for restarting the Japanese Overseas Cooperation Volunteers (JOCV) programme, which had been suspended since the COVID19 pandemic, and also for the ongoing Grassroots Human Security Grant Aid in the Maldives.

9. Minister Hayashi announced the intention to explore and study the possibility of a new project, which will symbolize the bilateral friendship, following the construction of the Sea Wall during the 1990’s.

10.Emphasising that the stability and prosperity of the Maldives is intrinsically linked to the peace and security of the Indian Ocean region and vice versa, both Foreign Ministers agreed to work closely to realize a “Free and Open Indo-Pacific”, and to strengthen dialogue and interactions, on diplomatic and security cooperation in this context.

11.Minister Shahid also highlighted the significant contributions of Japan through the Human Resource Development Scholarship Programme (JDS) and conveyed gratitude to the Government of Japan for their continuous support and partnership in these critical areas, which have had a profound and positive impact on the development and well-being of the Maldives.

12.Minister Shahid also expressed appreciation for the support rendered by the Government of Japan during his presidency at the 76th session of the United Nations General Assembly. Minister Hayashi also congratulated the Maldives on being elected to the UN Human Rights Council for the term 2023-2025.

13.Both Foreign Ministers agreed to work closely together at the United Nations and other international fora, on important issues of mutual interest, and to collaborate closely in addressing global challenges such as climate change.

14.Following the meeting, Minister Shahid and Minister Hayashi witnessed the exchange of Note Verbales between the Government of Maldives and the Government of Japan for the exemption of visa for Diplomatic and Official passports and the Exchange of Notes to provide a grant aid of One Hundred and Twenty Two Million Japanese Yen (approximately USD 1.1million) to the Maldives for the continuation of scholarship opportunities to be offered by the Government of Japan for the fiscal year 2023, under the Japanese Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship (JDS).

15.Both Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to further enhance the bilateral partnership between the Maldives and Japan, in various fields including economic and development cooperation as well as cooperation in the multilateral fora.

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan Hayashi Yoshimasa Departs Maldives after Official Visit
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan Hayashi Yoshimasa Departs Maldives after Official Visit
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan Hayashi Yoshimasa Departs Maldives after Official Visit

Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan, His Excellency Hayashi Yoshimasa departed today after concluding his two-day official visit to the Maldives.

During the visit, Minister Hayashi held bilateral discussions with Minister Shahid and called on the Minister of Defence, Uza. Mariya Ahmed Didi. Minister Hayashi also attended an official lunch hosted by Minister Shahid in his honour.

Both Minister Hayashi and Minister Shahid witnessed the Exchange of Notes under the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship [JDS] and the Exchange of Notes for the exemption of visa requirements for Diplomatic and Official passports for a period of 90 days. He also attended a Joint Handover Ceremony of a Fireboat and ICT Equipment for the Maldives National Defence Force (MNDF).

Minister Hayashi visited Kalaafaanu School which was built under the generous aid of the Government of Japan, and also to the Seawall Tetrapod Monument, which is a token of friendship and cooperation between Maldives and Japan.

Minister Hayashi was seen off at the Velana International Airport by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel and Senior Officials of the Ministry.

en.title: Foreign Minister of Japan visits Kalaafaanu School and the Seawall Tetrapod Monument during his official visit
en.description: Foreign Minister of Japan visits Kalaafaanu School and the Seawall Tetrapod Monument during his official visit
en.body:
Foreign Minister of Japan visits Kalaafaanu School and the Seawall Tetrapod Monument during his official visit

During his official visit to the Maldives, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan His Excellency Hayashi Yoshimasa visited Kalaafaanu School and the Seawall Tetrapod Monument in Male’.

Kalaafaanu School was built with grant aid from Government of Japan.  With the groundbreaking ceremony held on 16 February 1988., the project took less than eighteen months for completion, and Kalaafaanu School was officially inaugurated by Former President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom on 25 July 1989. Since its inauguration over 30 years ago, thousands of Maldivian students have graduated from Kalaafaanu School, many of whom are serving the nation in various sectors and distinguished positions in the Government.

The Male’ Seawall Construction Project was completed during the early 1990’s in four different phases and is the biggest project ever carried out by the Government of Japan under its Grant Aid Scheme. The Seawall Tetrapod Monument which is located in the South-East Side of Male’, is a token of friendship and cooperation between Maldives and Japan.

en.title: Exchange of Notes between Government of Maldives and Government of Japan
en.description: Exchange of Notes between the Government of Maldives and the Government of Japan
en.body:
Exchange of Notes between the Government of Maldives and the Government of Japan

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan, His Excellency Hayashi Yoshimasa today witnessed the Exchange of Notes between the Government of Maldives and the Government of Japan to provide a grant aid of One Hundred and Twenty Two Million Japanese Yen to the Maldives for the continuation of scholarships opportunities to be offered by the Government of Japan for the fiscal year 2023, under the Japanese Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship (JDS) and the Exchange of Notes for the exemption of visa requirements for Diplomatic and Official passports for a period of 90 days.

The Exchange of Notes for the visa requirements for Diplomatic and Official passports, is the first step that will eventually lead towards the waiving of visa requirements for all Maldivians.

The grant will provide 6 more scholarships again this year to the Maldivian students, a project which was implemented in August 2020, by the Government of Japan for further promoting the Human Resource Development in the Maldives.

The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel and the Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives Her Excellency Takeuchi Midori Exchanged the Notes at a ceremony held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Higher Education, Civil Service Commission, Maldives Immigration, Embassy of Japan and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) attended the ceremony.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid meets Foreign Minister of Japan Hayashi Yoshimasa
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid meets Foreign Minister of Japan, Hayashi Yoshimasa
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid meets Foreign Minister of Japan, Hayashi Yoshimasa

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan, His Excellency Hayashi Yoshimasa, held bilateral discussions today at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

During the Meeting, Minister Shahid welcomed Minister Hayashi and the delegation, to the Foreign Ministry and highlighted the enduring strength of the Maldives-Japan partnership and the close people-to-people engagement and friendship.

Both Foreign Minister Shahid, and Minister Hayashi reflected on the close historical relationship between Maldives and Japan and exchanged views on key areas of bilateral and multilateral interests. They agreed to work closely together on important issues of mutual interests, in further enhancing the close relations between the two countries.

Minister Shahid thanked Minister Hayashi and Japanese Government for the generous assistance that Japan has provided over nearly five decades of cooperation. He emphasized that the most visible impact of Japan's support within Male’ City is the Seawall, which is the most symbolic assistance provided by Japan. Minister Shahid also mentioned the significant role Japan played in the socio-economic development of the Maldives. He noted in particular, the contribution of Japan towards the expansion of the education services by building schools across the archipelago in the 1970s and 1980s; the technical assistance provided for the development of the fisheries industry; the assistance provided in establishing the telecommunications infrastructure which was vital for the growth of our tourism industry; and the contributions of Japan towards capacity building through the Human Resource Development Scholarship Programme. Minister Shahid expressed his appreciation to the Government of Japan for their continuous support and partnership in these critical areas, which have had a profound and positive impact on the development and well-being of the Maldives.

Minister Shahid expressed his gratitude to the Government and people of Japan for their generosity in providing the much-needed assistance to the Maldives during the COVID-19 pandemic by facilitating a crisis response emergency support loan of approximately USD 47 million and also donated 112,000 AstraZeneca vaccines to combat the pandemic.

Minister Shahid expressed appreciation for Japan’s recent assistance in the field of maritime security and reaffirmed the Government of Maldives’ strong commitment to the “Free and Open Indo-Pacific Plan (FOIP)” announced by Prime Minister Kishida in March this year.

Both Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen the partnership bilaterally, through economic and development cooperation and in the international for a by working together on global issues such as climate change, and cooperation to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals as well as international peace and security.

en.title: The Maldives submits a written statement to the ICJ with regard to the request for an Advisory Opinion on the legal consequences arising from the policies and practises of Israel in the occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem
en.description: The Maldives submits a written statement to the ICJ with regard to the request for an Advisory Opinion on the legal consequences arising from the policies and practises of Israel in the occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem
en.body:
The Maldives submits a written statement to the ICJ with regard to the request for an Advisory Opinion on the legal consequences arising from the policies and practises of Israel in the occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem

The Maldives has submitted a written statement to the International Court of Justice with regard to the request for an Advisory Opinion on the legal consequences arising from the policies and practises of Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem.

The request for an Advisory Opinion was made through resolution 77/247, which was passed during the 77th session of the United Nations General Assembly. The Maldives voted in favour of the resolution.

The statement was prepared by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Attorney General’s Office.

The Maldives has always stood in solidarity with the Palestinian people in their fight for self-determination and the realisation of an independent and sovereign State of Palestine established on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

THE END

Secretary (West) of the Ministry of External Affairs of India, Sanjay Verma, called on the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, today. The meeting was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

During the meeting, Minister Shahid emphasised on the importance of solidifying joint efforts in addressing the common security challenges to ensure peace and stability in both countries and the Indian Ocean region. They also discussed on further avenues to consolidate the ties of two countries in this area bilaterally and in the multilateral arena.

en.title: Maldives Delegation actively participated in the 53rd Session of the Human Rights Council
en.description: Maldives Delegation actively participated in the 53rd Session of the Human Rights Council
en.body:
Maldives Delegation actively participated in the 53rd Session of the Human Rights Council

The 53rd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council concluded in Geneva on Friday.

The Human Rights Council adopted 31 resolutions and the Delegation of Maldives delivered 32 national statements on an array of thematic areas. The Maldives co-sponsored 14 resolutions, including the Enhancement of international cooperation in the field of human rights, Contribution of development to the enjoyment of all human rights, Negative impact of corruption on the enjoyment of human rights and the mandate renewal of the Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities among others.

The Maldives was part of the cross-regional core group that drafted the resolution on the Mandate of the Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers. The main objective of this resolution is to renew the mandate of the Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers for a further period of three years. This resolution was adopted by consensus and had more than 71 co-sponsors supporting the resolution at the time of adoption. Further, in response to a request by the Organization for Islamic Cooperation (OIC), an urgent debate was held on 11th July with the purpose of bringing attention to the recent attacks on the sanctity of Holy Quran. The Maldives was a proud co-sponsor of the resolution titled “Countering religious hatred constituting incitement to discrimination, hostility or violence.” This resolution, adopted after the urgent debate at the 53rd Session, vehemently condemns the desecration of the Holy Quran.

The Maldives also co-sponsored 34 joint statements delivered at the Council. This included statements by the Organization for Islamic Cooperation among others. The Maldives on behalf of the group of Small Island Developing States (SIDS) delivered a statement at the Annual Panel Discussion on the theme of Adverse Impacts of Climate Change on the full realization of the right to food and reiterated SIDS commitment to work collectively to build resilient food systems that safeguard the right to food to ensure a sustainable future for all.

The Maldives Delegation at the 53rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council was led by H.E. Dr. Asim Ahmed, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary and Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Office at Geneva. As the Vice President of the Council, representing the Asia Pacific Group, Dr. Asim Ahmed chaired several meetings of the Council.

The Maldives and Egypt to hold the Second Round of Bilateral Political Consultations

The Maldives and Egypt will hold the Second Round of Bilateral Political Consultations on 16 July 2023 in Male’.

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel will lead the Political Consultations on behalf of the Government of Maldives. His Excellency Ambassador Ayman Kamel, Assistant Minister for Asian Affairs of the Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Egypt will co-chair the Political Consultations on behalf of the Government of Egypt.
